reason: This passage (Genesis 12) is narrated from an omniscient third-person perspective, not from a leader's point of view. More importantly, the text contains no narrative element of dealing with ungrateful people. The passage describes God's call to Abraham, His covenant promises, Abraham's obedience in departing with his household (Sarah, Lot, and their possessions), and his travels through Canaan. While Abraham is called to become a leader of a great nation, he is portrayed as obedient and faithful, not as dealing with ingratitude from those with him. The only people mentioned are his compliant family members and the Canaanites who merely inhabited the land—there is no conflict or ungratefulness depicted.
